paraphrases.text: If we find a material uncertainty, our report must flag it in the auditor's report and the related notes, and if those notes are inadequate we must modify our opinion.
Where a material uncertainty is identified, the auditor is required to highlight the related disclosures or, failing adequate disclosure, qualify the opinion.
Our findings rest on the audit evidence we gathered up to the date the auditor's report was issued.
The auditor's conclusions draw on evidence available at the report date.
Key audit matters are the issues that, in the auditor's judgement, were most important to the audit of the standalone statements for the current year.
The auditor identified as key audit matters those items of greatest significance to the standalone financial statements for the period.
The audit opinion does not extend to the other information in the report, and no assurance is given on it.
Other information included in the report falls outside the scope of the auditor's opinion, which provides no assurance on it.
Every related party transaction of the company and its subsidiaries is conducted on arm's length terms and within normal business practice.
The company and its subsidiaries carry out all dealings with related parties at arm's length, in the ordinary course of business.
The audit committee observed that the transactions in question are on arm's length terms and arise in the ordinary course of business.
The committee confirmed that the noted transactions were made at arm's length and in the normal course of business.
The stated limits apply even where the transactions form part of the company's ordinary business and are on arm's length terms.
Even transactions conducted in the ordinary course and at arm's length remain subject to these limits.
Transactions with related parties during the year were conducted in the ordinary course of business and at arm's length.
During the year, related party dealings took place in the normal course of business on arm's length terms.
Disclosure of transactions with related parties ends once the relationship no longer exists.
Related parties are disclosed only for as long as the relationship subsists.
No provision has been made for doubtful debts, and no amounts have been written off or back, in respect of balances due from or to related parties.
Related party balances carry no doubtful debt provision and no write-off or write-back has been recorded on them.
The promoters have not pledged any of their shares.
No promoter share pledging has taken place.
The shares are under a one-year lock-in and cannot be sold, transferred, or offered as security during that period.
During the lock-in period, the shares may not be transferred, marked with a lien, or pledged.
Future events or conditions could lead the company to stop operating as a going concern.
The company may be unable to continue as a going concern if future events or conditions so require.
No significant or material orders from regulators, courts or tribunals have affected the company's going concern status or future operations.
Regulators, courts and tribunals have issued no material orders that affect the going concern status or the company's future operations.
In managing capital, the company aims to protect its ability to remain a going concern and keep an optimal capital structure to maximise shareholder value.
Capital management seeks to preserve the company's going concern and an optimal capital structure, so as to maximise value for shareholders.
The annual accounts were prepared on the basis that the directors consider the company a going concern.
The directors prepared the annual accounts assuming the company will continue as a going concern.
The company has neither given nor received any guarantees in respect of related party receivables or payables.
No guarantees have been given or taken for amounts receivable from or payable to related parties.
The contingent liability estimates exclude any interest that counterparties might claim.
Interest that counterparties could claim is not included in the amounts assessed as contingent liabilities.
